text: Criterion is coverage. What type of coverage a wireless technology provides. Another possible criterion is, node mobility. What type of node mobility the technology supports. A third type of criterion is the network architecture that our technology supports. So let's first focus on coverage. If we choose as criterion to classify our wireless networks, the coverage, it means essentially the special area that our technology is able to cover. It is over which the technology will be able to provide service to our users. Here is a representation of what different technologies can do. So we have Bluetooth for example, that typically provides connectivity indoors. And this is the range of coverage of Bluetooth, that is order of meters. Then we have the Wi-Fi technologies. So when you see eight to two dot eleven, and then some letters, that's the name of the different types of Wi-Fi generations. We will explain that.
